info.title: JobRadar API
info.description: Job aggregation, per-user scoring and application tracking.

post.description:
Confirm an address from the emailed link.

Unauthenticated on purpose: people open these links in whichever browser
their mail client hands them, which is frequently not the one they are
signed in to.

Send another verification link to *your own* address.

Authenticated, and the address comes from the token rather than the body.
Taking it from the body would make this a way to mail arbitrary strangers
from your domain.
Returns an access token in the body and a refresh token in an httpOnly cookie.
Blacklist the refresh token and clear the cookie.

patch.description: Marks onboarding complete. No other field is writable here.

post.description:
Start a reset. Unauthenticated, by definition.

**Always answers 204**, whether or not the address belongs to an account.
Any difference — a different status, a different body, even a noticeably
different response time — turns this into an oracle for "is this person
registered?", which is precisely what `LoginView` already refuses to be.
Finish a reset with the emailed link.

Mint a new access token from the refresh cookie.

The token is read from the cookie, falling back to the body so the endpoint
is still usable from a non-browser client.

Create the account, its profile, and hand back tokens.

Registration returns tokens so the user lands straight in the app rather than
being bounced to a login form they just filled in.

PasswordResetConfirm.description:
A link plus the new password.

Validating the token here rather than in the view keeps the endpoint thin
and means a bad `uid`, a bad token and an expired token all surface the same
way — a 400 — without the view having to distinguish them. It should not
distinguish them: telling a caller *why* a link failed tells them whether
the account exists.

The refresh endpoint normally reads the httpOnly cookie.

The body field exists only so non-browser clients have a way in, and so the
schema describes something concrete.
